extracted.intended_audience: general news readers and news editors (wire-service audience)
extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service breaking-news dispatch reporting a military evacuation/operation, written for rapid distribution to newspapers and broadcasters; includes dateline, bylines, bulletins and multiple 'leads' for editioning. Emphasizes timeliness, sourcing, and operational detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and wire-service tag
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a city dateline, date and the wire-service identifier (e.g., "BOSTON, FEB. 6 (AP)-").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dateline appears at the top of each dispatch to locate the report and identify the reporting service; used repeatedly on separate dispatches within the same story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timed release / advance notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark embargo or advance status and release time (e.g., "FOR USE AT 7 P.M. EST, TODAY"; "AP FOREIGN SERVICE ADVANCE FOR PMS").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use explicit 'for use' or 'advance' lines to signal when copy may be published or which edition the advance is for; useful for editioning and newsroom scheduling.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead/version labeling (first/second/third lead, night lead)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide labeled lead variants for different editions (e.g., "SECOND NIGHT LEAD", "THIRD LEAD").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wire copy may include multiple prewritten leads so editors can choose the appropriate headline/angle for their edition; label them clearly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bulletin/urgent update format
rubrics_metrics.description: Use 'BULLETIN' (or similar) lines to signal immediate breaking updates with timestamp and short headline (e.g., "BULLETIN $ (AP)-THE FIRST TACHEN ISLANDS REFUGEE...").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bulletins are short, high-priority inserts to update or correct earlier copy; include time and succinct fact(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Attribution to correspondents and official sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Attribute information to named AP correspondents and to officials/positions (e.g., "AP correspondent Forrest Edwards reported from the 7th Fleet", "Adm. Alfred M. Pride said").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make clear who is reporting and the source of statements; attribute direct quotes to named individuals and positions to maintain credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of official communiqués and quoted statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Include and quote official communiqués, government statements and broadcasts when relevant (e.g., Navy communiqués, Peiping radio broadcasts, statements by Conant or Chiang).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present official language verbatim where possible and identify the issuing body; juxtapose with other sources when accounts conflict.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide concrete numeric and logistic details
rubrics_metrics.description: Report specific counts, distances and logistical facts (e.g., numbers of ships and planes, evacuee/troop totals, miles from mainland, tide heights, evacuation timelines).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise figures (ships: "75 warships", carriers: "6 carriers", evacuees: "about 30,000") and operational details lend authority and situational clarity; include units and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Report operational constraints and hazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe operational difficulties and hazards affecting the event (e.g., mined waters, rocky beaches, 16–18 foot tides, need for minesweepers and demolition teams).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain practical issues shaping the operation to help readers understand difficulty, pace and risk; report on measures taken to mitigate hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present conflicting accounts and propaganda claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When sources disagree, report the differing versions (e.g., AP correspondents saw no loading until today vs. Peiping radio's account; Red broadcasts calling actions 'military provocation').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show rather than resolve disputes: attribute contrasting claims to their sources and note where independent confirmation is lacking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contextual and historical background
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide larger political and historical context to the specific event (e.g., links to Paris treaties, post-World War II ambassadorial status, reference to Inchon landing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief background helps readers place the immediate dispatch in a broader strategic or historical frame; include only concise, relevant context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Descriptive scene-setting and human detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Use vivid descriptive detail and human-interest elements (e.g., descriptions of radar scopes, sailors' actions, refugees' placards) to convey atmosphere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interleave operational facts with on-the-ground color to engage readers while maintaining factual reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wire-style internal codes and editing marks
rubrics_metrics.description: Include wire-specific metadata and internal codes (e.g., block capitals for headlines, editorial codes like 'CK1124PPs', editioning notes 'END ADVAN').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These markers signal editorial handling, version control, and internal processes; preserve them in wire copy but editors may strip for publication.
